items.text: JB Pritzker is the Democratic governor seeking a third term. His running mate Christian Mitchell is a former state representative, deputy governor and University of Chicago vice president, and serves as a first lieutenant in the Illinois Air National Guard.

sentences.text: JB Pritzker is the Democratic governor seeking a third term.
His running mate Christian Mitchell is a former state representative, deputy governor and University of Chicago vice president, and serves as a first lieutenant in the Illinois Air National Guard.

items.text: The campaign focuses on lowering costs for families. Pritzker says he has made Illinois more affordable by eliminating the state sales tax on groceries, doubling the child tax credit and lowering prescription drug prices. He opposes using one-time legal settlement funds for ongoing budget gaps like the Chicago school deficit. Mitchell says he will carry out the governor's agenda to lower costs and raise wages. Pritzker supports the state ban on assault weapons and high-capacity magazines, and Mitchell has advocated for universal background checks. Pritzker says Illinois should not let data centers drive up electricity bills, put pressure on water supplies or override local concerns. In 2017, Mitchell co-sponsored legislation to direct over $200 million to needy school districts. The campaign pledges to protect reproductive rights.

items.text: During Pritzker's tenure, Illinois raised the minimum wage toward $15. The state also legalized recreational cannabis and set clean energy goals. As deputy governor, Mitchell led a $45 billion infrastructure plan through the state legislature. He also served as the legislative lead on the state assault weapons ban after the Highland Park shooting. In 2024, Pritzker authorized the state employee health insurance plan to cover GLP-1 drugs. He also signed legislation to regulate high-speed e-bikes and e-scooters.
